sources.cite: Python 3.15 documentation, The Python Tutorial, 6. Modules (6.1.2 The Module Search Path)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. 'The directory containing the script being run is placed at the beginning of the search path, ahead of the standard library path. This means that scripts in that directory will be loaded instead of modules of the same name in the library directory. This is an error unless the replacement is intended.'

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: The running script's directory is first on sys.path, so a local statistics.py is loaded instead of the standard library module; dir() and __file__ show it.

parts.label: What you changed
parts.criteria: Rename the local module so it no longer clashes; a wildcard import from inside the same-named file or reordering sys.path only moves the problem.

parts.criteria: statistics.__file__ points to the library and the report matches the booking system.

right.headline: Good: find the file, then the fix
right.body: When a module lacks a name it should have, ask which file was imported. The script's folder comes first on sys.path, so a same-named file wins.

scoring.modelReasoning: 'module statistics has no attribute mean' means the module imported is not the one expected. statistics.__file__ and dir(statistics) show reports/statistics.py: the directory of the running script is placed ahead of the standard library on sys.path, so a local file with a library module's name shadows it. Rename the local file; a wildcard import inside it or a reordered sys.path keeps or spreads the clash.
